title: ED Discharge for Patients With Limited English Proficiency
summary: Improve ED discharge communication with qualified interpretation, clear return precautions, medication review, teach-back, and follow-up.
body_markdown:
###


No. Studies have reported different associations across populations and health systems, and many clinical and access factors affect returns. Measure discharge communication directly instead of treating language as the sole cause.


###


Use approved language support for the discharge conversation whenever a language barrier could limit meaningful communication, even if interpretation was already used during triage or evaluation.


###


Include the specific symptom or change, relevant threshold or timing, and the action the patient should take, such as calling a clinician, returning to the ED, or calling emergency services.


###


Use teach-back for the first steps at home, medication use, return precautions, follow-up, and pending results. Reteach and check again when the response differs from the plan.


###


Track language-data accuracy, interpretation use, translated instructions, failures, medication discrepancies, teach-back, pending-result ownership, scheduled follow-up, complaints, and reviewed return visits.
